newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy telecom bill likely in lower house next week.
newsitem.headline: Italy telecom bill likely in lower house next week.

text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) is likely to start discussing a bill paving the way for privatisation of state telecoms group Stet next week, a parliamentary official said on Tuesday.
The bill, which creates a regulatory watchdog for the telecoms sector, had been due to be examined on Tuesday.

But the government asked for a postponement "for scheduling reasons", said Giuseppe Giulietti, a member of the Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest party in government. He said the bill would "probably be discussed next week".
Telecoms holding Stet is due to merge on Friday with its main operating unit Telecom Italia. The new enlarged group will be called Telecom Italia and it is scheduled for privatisation in mid October.
The sale cannot proceed until the watchdog has been set up.
The government has already set out the guidelines for the privatisation of Telecom Italia in a separate decree.
Giulietti said the watchdog bill was likely to go to the Senate (upper house) for final approval at the end of the month.
